Finally found it:

Well, let's assume that happens in a scenario where Halvidar never becomes President, and the MSIF becomes a legitimate political party on Mars making it next to impossible for the colonials to join the war. 

Mexico would retake the Southwest in short order, and probably push their military into Louisiana and the great plains just to make a point. The war would last much longer in this timeline without the devastating tactics of the Colonies, probably into the mid 2140s, and it would end with the US Suing for peace and ceding most of Aztlan's territory to Mexico.

Mexico would consolidate their gains around the world where the US could not hope for a serious victory. A new Chinese Confederacy of sorts would form out of Mexican client states in China and India would be partitioned far more drastically. The Poles would control Northern Europe, bringing the American nightmare to fruition, however the decline in European populations and scarcity of resources would make this far less of a threat than such a scenario would be today. Mexico would establish an alliance of Southern European states in a kind of Neo MU to counter the Poles, sewing up North Africa in the alliance as well. The Beanstalk elevator would remain in American hands, but the Uganada Tower would become an international facility controlled by the locals, while Mexico would informally control the Ecuador tower.

Mexico would become the world's most powerful nation-state on Earth by war's end, and over the next century the US would begin to fragment. First, the colonies would break off, almost immediately after Mexico declares victory. Mars would be the most powerful and most unified by far, while the Jovians and Titans would be somewhere between independent and somewhere between US and Martian colonies. The US would maintain control over much of the Moon, but Mexico would have taken a sizable portion of the territory, as well as several asteroid bases. On Earth, the US would remain united, but separatism would rise with Mexican control over Texas and there's likely be a Forth-Mexican American War over the Port of Louisiana, involving Cascadian, possibly even Neo-Confederate/Southron separatists. But the Truth is with control over Texas and the Carribean Mexico would be the real power in North America from that point forward. The real struggle on the international stage would between the Poles and the Martians.

As the United States recedes, Mars would rise to fill the void in Space. Venus would be a Martian Colony, and the Interplanetary Trade Commission would become a kind of interplanetary NATO with Mars and Titan being the two most important members. Eventually the American Lunar colonies would look more toward Mars for their security than on Earth, and while Mexico would be the most powerful country on Earth, Mars would be the most powerful country period, and would begin playing a greater role in Earth politics after Mexico seizes control of the elevators. Beanstalk would eventually be transferred to Mars, probably in a sale by the US. Australia (independent by this point) and Oceania would be ground zero for Martian influence on Earth, along with what remained of US backed China and East Africa. The influence would be very informal for the first 50 years of Pax-Mexicana, but eventually the two powers would come to blows over either former American colonies around Earth or the Moon. Poland would be a Martian ally in that war, and Mars would win. 

The First Interplanetary War, would be relatively small, but it would end with Martian control over most American territory around the Earth and on the Moon, and Mars annexing Australia and most of the former American territories in Oceania (which would have been independent for some time or owned by Mexico). Mars would also either annex East Africa outright or simply declare them to be a protectorate. An Interplanetary Cold War would define the next half century, with Mexico and Mars grappling for control of equatorial territory and allies. But Mars would have the advantage of a massive population and most of the resources of the Solar System.
